newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees difficult questions after NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees difficult questions after NATO talks.

text.p: The Russian Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that differences still prevented Moscow from signing a deal on future relations with the NATO alliance.

A brief foreign ministry statement issued after talks between minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on Tuesday said the two sides had come closer on some issues. But it added: "Some difficult questions remain which must be resolved to pave the way for a mutually acceptable document on relations between Russia and NATO".
The statement said consultations between Russia and NATO would continue.
Russia is seeking a deal with NATO to prevent the military infrastructure of the Western alliance from moving nearer its borders when NATO brings in Eastern European countries as new members.
Moscow also wants a say in aspects of NATO activities which it says concern its security.
NATO says it is ready to meet some of Russia's security concerns in a loose charter. But it appears reluctant to accept any conditions which would affect rights of the new members.
